pageCache.pageTitle: British Values | St Joseph’s Catholic Primary & Nursery School
pageCache.text:
British Values
British Values
British Values at St Joseph's
The DFE have recently reinforced the need for schools to encourage pupils to respect British values of:
and Ofsted reflect this in their expectations that schools must "promote preparation for, and an appreciation of life in modern Britain".
Exploring religious and different social beliefs, in a peaceful and non-violent way and learning how to show respect for those with different ideas, cultures and traditions, is a valuable part of growing up and something we encourage. We endeavour to protect children from extremist and violent views that are contrary to these aims.
St Joseph's Nursery - British Values
As part of our focus on democracy we have been voting on our favourite fruits and food. We have made graphs using the 2Count program on the computer to record our results as well as voting to select our favourite snack time fruit. In the Autumn term we worked together to devise a set of Class rules and we have been reminding each other what they are to try and not break them.
In Reception class we have been looking at British values in our topic and circle time. As a class we talk about how and why we should treat others equally and with respect. We discuss in groups about decision making and understanding what is right and what is wrong. In RE, we enjoy learning about other cultures and beliefs and learning to respect people's differences. Most of all we try our best to help one another at all times.
In year 2 we have been learning all about British Values. We have been comparing British life to that of other countries. We have been learning about the consequences of our actions and how to be a good citizen.
In year 4 British Values runs through the core of our learning. Rights, responsibilities and respect are very important to us. We enjoy discussing how our society is different to those in the past and those in other countries too.
In yr 5 we have been comparing British life with life in Ghana.
We have been working on fair trade.
Through this topic, we have been looking at mutual respect and democracy.

Dunstan Catholic Educational Trust
St Joseph's Catholic Primary school are proud to be part of the Dunstan Catholic Educational Trust, which was incorporated on the 1st March 2022. The Trust consists of 10 schools serving the Catholic Diocese of Clifton. St Joseph's joined the Trust in March 2022 and works closely with all the schools in the Trust. Formal Consultation Questionnaire
The Dunstan Partnership is a group of Catholic schools in Somerset and North Somerset created with the aim of supporting and strengthening Catholic schools through collaboration and sharing of good practice
The purpose of this partnership is to ensure that all schools within the Dunstan Partnership provide high quality Catholic education that serves the need of its community. The principle responsibilities will be to support the Bishop in ensuring that all schools provide a distinctive education based on the theology and philosophy of Catholicism. The overarching aim of the group will be to fulfill the Bishop's Diocesan vision of:
Deepening Prayer, Enabling Communion, Strengthening Mission
Responsibilities also include the monitoring, reviewing and reporting on all matters concerned with raising standards and improving the quality of teaching and learning across the partnership as well as all matters concerned with resources that can be obtained across the partnership to increase our buying power.

pageCache.text:
Welcome
Mrs Rebecca Suik - Headteacher
Welcome to St Joseph's Catholic Primary School and Nursery.
St Joseph's joined the Dunstan Catholic Educational Trust in March 2022 and we are proud to be part of our community of Catholic Schools.
I hope that your association with the School will be happy and provide a safe learning environment for your children. As a Catholic school, we aim to develop our pupils' knowledge and understanding of our faith, while promoting Christian values in all aspects of daily life.
We strive to enable individual children to reach their full potential. The education of each child is based on a partnership between the School and home and rooted in the Gospel Values. Christ is at the centre of all that we do. We are extremely proud of all that goes on here. The children at St Joseph's are supported in their learning by dedicated staff, governors and parents. Our website is just a small window into life at St Joseph's School. We are proud of our high academic achievements as well as our participation in the arts, sporting activities and parish life.
I encourage you to browse around our website, where you will find details of school events, visitors and activities that serve to enliven the curriculum, alongside information about our breakfast and after school clubs. There are also many extra curricular activities on offer to your children. Please always feel free to make personal contact with the school, where you will always be most welcome. Thank you for visiting!

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club | St Joseph’s Catholic Primary & Nursery School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
Welcome to our Breakfast Club
We have successfully been running our Breakfast Club since September 2009. We operate the Breakfast Club daily during term time, for children attending St Joseph’s Catholic Primary and Nursery School.
The club runs from 7:45am. Key Stage 1 and 2 children go into the playground at 8:45 where a member of staff will be on duty. The Nursery children are supervised until 9am when they are escorted into Nursery.
The Breakfast club is led by Miss Jacqui Cooper and supported by Mrs Sian Price. All of our staff are DBS checked and already work within the school in various roles.
There are limited spaces available each day at a cost of £4.90 per child per session (or part of) and £4.40 for each additional sibling. Places are allocated on a first come first served basis. These can be booked in advance via MCAS My Child at School, however if it says the session is full please contact the school office on 01278 784641 and we will endeavour to extend the staffing level to accommodate additional children. Payment for all bookings must be received through your MCAS My Child at School Account prior to attendance of the Breakfast Club.
A registration form MUST be completed with contact details for emergencies prior to your child’s first booking.
A member of staff will come out to take your child / children from you at the start of the Breakfast Club session.
During the hour children will receive a breakfast that will include a selection from, cereals, toast, pancakes, waffles, fresh fruit, croissants plus hot or cold drinks. If your child has a favourite cereal let us know and we will endeavour to provide it. Breakfast will be served between 7:45am and 8:20am. Your child must arrive before 8:15am if they require breakfast.
In the remaining time children will be engaged in a range of activities which will be based on play and relaxation, and not school work, although the staff will be happy to assist with any homework during the session.
Should you wish to apply for a place/s in the Breakfast club, please complete a Breakfast Club Registration form prior to making your booking on MCAS My Child at School.

French
Learning
French - Intent, implementation and impact.
French - progression documents
What will your children learn from this PlanIt KS2 French scheme?
This KS2 French scheme of work covers four fantastic units:
By the end of this unit your children will be able to talk about the various places in a town, give helpful directions and speak about maths and numbers. Your children will also gain a better understanding for grammatical structures and features of the French language.
This KS2 French unit will teach your children key vocabulary and phrases to do with shopping, colours and clothes. They will also gain a deeper understanding for French culture by acting out a shopping role-play activity.
One major benefit of learning a language is being able to appreciate different cultures and countries. So, with this unit your children will be able to put their KS2 French to good use as they learn about France’s capital city, French landmarks and French people. They will also be able to talk about their own country and nationality in French.
This unit is all to do with telling the time and talking about what you do during the day. Children will learn how to read a timetable in French and discuss their school schedule.
These 4 themes are split into 6 topics in years 3-5 and 4 topics in year 6.

History and Geography
Learning
History and Geography
"In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth"
(Genesis 1:1)
"Remember the days of old; consider the years of many generations" (Deuteronomy 32:7)
History immerses pupils in unfamiliar worlds, and in the diversity and commonality of human experience across time and place. At the same time, history helps pupils to make sense of their own experiences, and of the world they inhabit. The study of history is complex and constantly evolving through new approaches, new lenses and new evidence. Every pupil is entitled to encounters with the richness of the past and the complexity of historical enquiry. (Ofsted Rich Encounters with the past: History Subject Report)
‘Professor Alistair Bonnett describes geography as ‘the world discipline’, an unwieldy yet utterly necessary and very human project to seek order and meaning in the diversity and complexity of the world. (The Geographical Association)

2019 Ofsted History Deep Dive
November 2025- Burnham on Sea Remembrance Parade. Today a selection of our children from across the School took part in our local Remembrance Sunday Parade representing St Joseph's. They joined the Parade of Ex & Current Servicemen/women and other local organisations and Schools to the War Memorial Hospital. They then laid a Poppy Wreath on behalf of the School and were fantastic representatives!
Year 4 History - Today we took part in a ‘Historical Sources Treasure Hunt’, where we looked at a variety of secondary sources about Alfred the Great, and assessed whether it was written with bias.
January 2025 - The year five class visited Somerset museum for a set of Tudor workshops. It fitted perfectly with the unit of work they have been doing in class. They made Tudor soap, learnt how to write with a quill and visited the Tudor Almshouse.
As part of Holocaust Memorial Week we learnt about a "Frank Foley". Frank went to St Joseph's and we found out more about the key role he played in WW2.
Marking Holocaust Memorial Day with a local link. We joined together to celebrate the life of Francis “Frank” Foley who worked for M16 and saved many Jews from death. He was a local man, who lived in Highbridge and came to St. Joseph’s school. A road in the town is named after him. The year five children created PowerPoints showing his legacy.
January 2025 - Year 4 are loving using our artefacts from the Museum Service, along with our history books from the library, to create fact files on Anglo-Saxon settlements.
Remembrance Day- Today we gathered together as a whole school community to take part in a special Remembrance Service and Silence to remember those who have lost their lives at war. Lots of children wore their uniforms from Guides, Brownies and Scouts out of respect too!
November 2024- One of our Reception Children and a Year 5 Pupil took part in the Burnham-on-Sea Remembrance Parade on behalf of St Joseph's. They joined the Parade of Ex & Current Servicemen/women and other local organisations and Schools to the War Memorial Hospital. They then laid a Poppy Wreath on behalf of the School and were fantastic representatives!
October 2024 - Year 4 had a fantastic Victorians workshop on Tuesday, where they experienced what life would have been like in Victorian schools. They dressed up as school children, followed traditional rules, practised writing on chalk boards, learnt how to sew, and even investigated Victorian artefacts! One child said “it was so special to figure out how Victorian children lived and behaved all those years ago. It was so fun, but we had to be very well behaved!”
October 2024- Some of the Key Stage 2 Classes have had some artefacts delivered from the Museum Service based around their units of The Vikings and The Victorians! The children will use these in their learning over the coming weeks!
September 2024- Year 5 have been exploring different photographic sources of evidence to deduce how they might be linked to The Vikings! They drew from prior knowledge and linked the photographs to trade routes. We then introduced the new learning of Viking Sagas and discovered the photographs were linked to Leif Erikson and The Saga of the Discover of Vinland!
September 2024- Year 3 visited The Museum of Somerset to learn more about The Iron Age! The children could use key historical vocabulary such as 'artefact' and 'archaeology' to explain about the knowledge they had of the Iron Age so far! They took part in re-enactment activities where they dressed up, had a go at coin striking and learnt about the Meare Lake Beads! The children linked their learning to their locality and discovered that Meare Lake was a popular production site for beads during the Iron Age!
September 2024- The Reception children have been asked to bring in photographs of their families and of them as babies! The children have been reflecting on early memories and experiences that they have had using their familiar pictures! They have been looking at the similarities and differences between then and now helping to develop their understanding of the world!
